title: Holding More Than One Optional Supplemental Benefit Rider
content:
A member of a Ridgecrest medical plan may hold up to the tier's maximum number of Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders at once, so that somebody who wants both a dental and a vision rider is served rather than made to choose. The maximum one member may hold at once is 2 on five of the riders and 1 on the bundle rider.

## The duplicate condition

No rider of the same official name is already in force for this member in the same benefit year, standing at requested, in its waiting period, active or suspended for unpaid premium. This condition is judged before a rider request is taken, on the member's own rider records — their identifying number, the official name of each rider, the benefit year it belongs to and the standing of each one. The correlation is to the member: it is that member's own rider records that are looked at, and a rider of the same name held by somebody else is nothing to the matter. What decides the question is what those records show, and two rider records that differ in their benefit year or in the day the rider took effect are separate records rather than one repeated.

## The bundle rider

The bundle rider is a single rider in its own right and may never be held alongside another rider, because it already covers dental, vision and hearing.

## Riders in different benefit years

Riders in different benefit years are not duplicates, and a member's history usually shows one ended rider record for each year they held it.

## Where the maximum is already held

Where the member already holds the maximum, a further rider is taken only after one is cancelled, and the member is told what the minimum holding period on the existing rider means for that.

## Points of judgement

**A rider standing at requested counts toward the maximum.** The four standings that make a rider one already in force for this purpose are requested, in its waiting period, active, and suspended for unpaid premium. A rider that has been ended is not among them.

**The same official name is what makes a duplicate.** Two riders of different official names held in the same benefit year are not duplicates of one another; what they cover is not the test.

**The member's own recollection is not the record.** The question is decided on the member's rider records as they stand, not on what the member says they hold.
